intro: San Antonio listings advertise non-climate 10x10 units from about $27, while typical street rates run about $90–$98/month. Metro asking rents are down about 5% year over year and more supply is still opening, but once the move-in special ends and the first existing-customer increase lands, the six-month average still clears the advertised rate.

units.notes: Locker / closet size. Fixed fees dominate the true cost at this size. Non-climate listings from about $20; climate-controlled from about $13. Climate-controlled street rate ~$42.
Walk-in closet; studio overflow. No reliable lowest-promo figure published for this size (gap). Climate-controlled ~$62.

Most rented size. City average $97, down 3% YoY (StorageCafe, Sep 2026); StorageUnitCosts lists $98, down 2.0% YoY (Aug 2026). San Antonio metro averages $90, down 5.1% YoY (Storage Stats). Climate-controlled ~$106.
Two-bedroom contents. Estimate: single source (StorageCafe, Sep 2026). Climate-controlled ~$146.
Three-bedroom home or a car. Climate-controlled ~$189. Non-climate listings from about $45.

local_tips: StorageCafe lists Dignowity Hill (~$72), Nogalitos–South Zarzamora (~$82) and Ingram Hills (~$85) among the cheapest areas, while Forest Crest (~$261) and Midtown (~$250) run highest.
San Antonio's all-unit average is lowest around December (~$139) and highest in August (~$142), StorageCafe — a small seasonal gap, so compare facilities rather than waiting for a cheaper month.
About 589,000 sq ft of new storage is due in 2026 across 8 facilities (StorageCafe), after 844,000 sq ft opened in 2025. Newer buildings often lead with a steep move-in rate; ask what month 5 costs.
The metro has roughly 9.4 sq ft of storage per person and 600+ facilities (Storage Stats), so a second and third quote are easy to get.
Extra Space charges a $50 admin fee (per StorageUnitCosts), higher than our $29 default; adjust the calculator if your facility charges more.
